scenarios.title: Lab smoke: owned queue, bounded send
scenarios.summary: Creates one owned anycast queue lab.<runId>.smoke on the verified lab broker and sends a bounded number of deterministic text messages to it, each with labRun and labSeq properties.
scenarios.expected: Fixture assertion: the queue's messageCount reaches the number sent before the readiness deadline. In Artemis Browser: the queue appears on /overview with that count, and /broker reports the node id the lab recorded. Cleanup removes exactly the queue and its address.

scenarios.title: Basic queues and connection
scenarios.summary: Empty and populated queues with distinct waiting, delivering, scheduled, added, acked, expired and killed counts; names with spaces, & and Unicode; 0, 1 and 251 persistent messages with sequence properties.
scenarios.expected: Overview counters, sorting and filters, paging and refresh match independent lab readings.

scenarios.title: Message bodies and export content
scenarios.summary: Text, bytes, map, stream, object and empty bodies; typed properties; Unicode, quotes, newlines, literal HTML; long and large (250KB) bodies; values beginning =, +, - and @.
scenarios.expected: Detail, previews, large badges, downloads and CSV/JSON exports agree with the send manifest; CSV neutralises formulas.

scenarios.title: Filters, search and export bounds
scenarios.summary: 300 messages with a late marker at positions 251-260, distinct priority, durability and timestamps; matches across two queues; known exact IDs.
scenarios.expected: Core filters, cross-queue search, match caps and export limits behave as documented.

scenarios.title: Scheduled, held, redelivered, dead-lettered and expired
scenarios.summary: Scheduled messages; consumers holding deliveries unacknowledged; rollback until dead-lettered; TTL expiry; missing dead-letter and expiry destinations.
scenarios.expected: Scheduled and in-flight panels, budgets, Diagnose findings and killed/expired counters match the lab's record.

scenarios.title: Routing, subscriptions and diverts
scenarios.summary: Anycast queue named differently from its address; multicast feed with durable, filtered, shared and non-durable subscriptions; exclusive and non-exclusive diverts; unrouted sends.
scenarios.expected: Address view, FQQN browsing, subscription lag and divert links are correct.

scenarios.title: Clients and rates
scenarios.summary: Identified and anonymous producers and consumers with several sessions; bounded target-rate traffic; restart or recreation for counter discontinuities.
scenarios.expected: Broker, client drilldown and rates agree with actual operation counts; no fabricated throughput across resets.

scenarios.title: Queue behavior
scenarios.summary: Paused and browse-only queues; last-value, ring, non-destructive and purge-on-no-consumers; exclusive, grouped and dispatch-gated consumers.
scenarios.expected: Effective settings and behavior findings explain what the counters show.

scenarios.title: Address pressure
scenarios.summary: Low-limit addresses under PAGE, BLOCK, FAIL and DROP; an operator block; reduced global memory and disk thresholds in an isolated profile.
scenarios.expected: Usage, policy and observed versus inferred findings match independently measured results.

scenarios.title: Permissions and interruption
scenarios.summary: Restricted viewer with management RBAC set at startup; a user without manage; the owned broker stopped and restarted under Browser.
scenarios.expected: Panels fail independently and explain why; connection loss is explicit and recovery works.

scenarios.title: Scale and responsiveness
scenarios.summary: A small preset, then up to 100,000 bounded small messages, many queues, clients, subscriptions and held deliveries within the lab's budgets.
scenarios.expected: Pages stay responsive and correct; the non-destructive guarantee holds.

scenarios.title: External harness: login, host, TLS and deployment
scenarios.summary: Not broker traffic: Browser profiles for loopback without login, configured login, hostile Host header, missing CSRF token, non-loopback startup, and the Helm deployment.
scenarios.expected: Documented as a harness procedure rather than a lab recipe.
